The file is copied verbatim; do not hand-edit it. To update, copy the new
`dist/softfloat64.metal` from the upstream repository, re-run
`shasum -a 256`, and refresh this table.

## How it is used

`sf64_core.h` (one directory up) builds the `sf64` type and the `sf::`
namespace on top of the packed bit-pattern API only
(`__softfloat64_fadd/fsub/fmul/fdiv/fsqrt/fma`, the `cvt_*` conversions and
`feq/flt/fle/fgt/fge`), always with rounding mode 0
(nearest-ties-to-even) and without `SOFTFLOAT_FTZ`. The unpacked
`__softfloat64_unp_*` API is not used (it is documented upstream as unsafe
with zeros). The amalgamated shader source places this file first; the
downstream headers contain no `#include` of it.

## Measured deviations at this commit (`tests/metal/test_sf64_core.py`)

- The file header says `fdiv`/`fsqrt` flush subnormal *outputs* to zero. Measured:
  `fdiv` produces correctly rounded subnormal outputs (20k random cases,
  `test_div_subnormal_output`); `fsqrt` cannot produce subnormals. The comment
  is stale, not the code.
- `__softfloat64_cvt_f64_to_f32(x, 0)` returns 0 for |x| in (2^-150, 2^-149),
  which must round up to the smallest float32 subnormal (2^-149). `sf::to_float`
  therefore implements the conversion itself.
- `__softfloat64_cvt_f64_to_i64(x, 0)` (nearest-even) adds 1 to odd integers in
  [2^52, 2^53) (the `dropped == tie == 0 && odd` branch). Mode 3 (truncation,
  used by `sf::to_long`) is unaffected; `sf::to_long_rint` goes through the exact
  `sf::rint` instead.

All arithmetic entry points (`fadd/fsub/fmul/fdiv/fsqrt/fma`), `cvt_f32_to_f64`,
`cvt_i64_to_f64` and the comparisons were bit-exact against NumPy float64 /
exact rational references on ~1e6 random and special inputs.
